main_text.p: solutum est. Quo perfecto aliam fossam parem fodit, non multum a priore difsun-ctam, spectantem ad mediterranea: ad-diditque duas praterea alias illis similes, & circumpositas, ita ut totum opus fos-sionis fieret quadrangulum, omnesque ejus partes muniit vallis acutis: & post val-los fossas altas vallumq; castrensè duxit.

Ea vero parte, qua Carthaginem spectabat, murum etiam extruxit xxv stadiorum longitudine, altitudine pedum xii, prater propugnacula & turres, qua per intervalla muro imminebant: latitudo seu crassities muri dimidium altitudinis aquabat. In medio turris erant altissima tecta quadruplici fastigio ligneo, unde despicere licebat ea, quae in urbe fierent. His operibus totius exercitus labore[illegible, ~4 letters] absolutis intra dies noctesque viginti quatuor, militibus vicissim nunc arma tenentibus nunc opus facientibus, nec cibum nec somnium nisi necessarium capientibus, in his castris collocavit copias: praebuitque ei hoc opus tum castrorum usum, tum munitionum contra hostes[illegible, ~5 letters] extensarum. Hinc enim erumpens commeatum, qui a terra iis afferebatur, Carthaginiensibus adimebat. Nam hac sola cervice exceptâ reliqua omnis urbs[illegible, ~4 letters] undiq; circumluebatur. Atque haec prima, ac maximè famis malorumque causa ob-[illegible, ~3 letters]sessis

page.notes: Right-margin notes are too faint and small to read reliably; they are marked as illegible at their approximate positions, with letter counts estimated. Left-margin marks and the reversed show-through text are not printed text on this page and were omitted. The word "sessis" at the start of the last line is the continuation of "ob-" from the line above and is transcribed as "ob-sessis". The "ɔc"-like marks on the right edge look like printer's or scanner marks and were omitted.
